# Planning GeoAI Investments

GeoAI programs require sustained investment across data, compute, talent, and tooling. But the single biggest driver of what you need to invest in — and how much — is the **decision tempo** your use cases require.

::: {.callout-important}
## Connection to the Decision Filter
This chapter expands on [Decision Filter Q3: What decision latency must this serve?](five-questions.qmd#q3-tempo) The difference between a quarterly planning model and a real-time routing engine isn't just speed — it's a fundamentally different cost structure, team shape, and infrastructure stack. Pick the tempo first, then architect.
:::

## Key Questions

1. **What decision tempo do our prioritized use cases require?** Strategic (weeks-months), tactical (hours-days), operational (minutes), or embedded (milliseconds)? Each tempo tier has a different cost profile.
2. **Are we building for one tempo or multiple?** Mixed-tempo programs need separate infrastructure tracks — a single pipeline cannot serve a quarterly planning model and a real-time operational system.
3. **How do we phase investment to deliver value incrementally?** Start at the tempo that delivers the most value with the least infrastructure risk.
4. **How do we measure return on investment for GeoAI?** ROI metrics should connect directly to the decision being improved, not to technical outputs.

## Matching Investment to Tempo

| Tempo | Infrastructure Needs | Team Shape | Annual Cost Range | Time to First Value |
|-------|---------------------|------------|------------------|-------------------|
| **Strategic** (weeks-months) | Batch compute, analyst workstations, data warehouse | Small: 2-3 analysts + 1 data engineer | Low-moderate | 3-6 months |
| **Tactical** (hours-days) | Near-real-time pipelines, cloud compute, model serving | Medium: data engineers + ML engineers + domain experts | Moderate | 6-12 months |
| **Operational** (minutes) | Streaming infrastructure, low-latency APIs, monitoring | Large: full MLOps team + SRE + domain experts | High | 12-18 months |
| **Embedded** (milliseconds) | Edge compute, specialized hardware, on-device inference | Specialized: embedded systems + ML optimization | Very high | 18+ months |

::: {.callout-warning}
## The Mismatch Trap
The most common investment mistake is building operational-tempo infrastructure for strategic-tempo use cases. A quarterly site-selection model doesn't need streaming Kafka pipelines and GPU-backed inference endpoints. That's not engineering excellence — it's waste that creates ongoing maintenance burden. Conversely, underbuilding for operational tempo means your demo works but your production system fails under real-world latency requirements.
:::

## Investment Categories

| Category | Examples | Cost Drivers |
|----------|----------|-------------|
| **Data** | Imagery subscriptions, labeling services | Resolution, coverage, frequency, exclusivity |
| **Compute** | Cloud GPU instances, training clusters | Model size, experiment volume, inference tempo |
| **Talent** | Hiring, training, contractors | Market rates, retention, team topology |
| **Tooling** | MLOps platforms, annotation tools | Build vs. buy decisions |
| **Governance** | Audit processes, compliance tooling | Regulatory requirements, error cost tolerance |

## Phased Roadmap Template

### Phase 1: Foundation (Months 1-6)

**Goal:** Validate the highest-priority use case at the right tempo with the smallest defensible investment.

- Establish governance framework
- Conduct data moat audit (see [Data Strategy](data-strategy.qmd))
- Hire or designate core team
- Complete 1-2 proof-of-concept projects at the tempo your use case requires
- Identify the specific person/role who will act on model outputs (see [Decision Filter Q4](five-questions.qmd#q4-adoption))

### Phase 2: Scale (Months 7-18)

**Goal:** Move validated use cases to production and establish infrastructure for the confirmed tempo tier.

- Deploy first production model(s) with feedback loops
- Build reusable data pipelines matched to required latency
- Establish model registry and MLOps practices
- Measure and report on decision-quality metrics (not just model accuracy)
- Expand team and training

### Phase 3: Optimize (Months 18+)

**Goal:** Expand to additional use cases, potentially at different tempo tiers.

- Optimize model performance and cost
- Expand to additional use cases (each passing the five-question filter)
- Build self-service capabilities for analysts
- Evaluate whether new use cases require a different tempo tier (and therefore different infrastructure)
